gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Samsung's own US store charged $999.99 for the 128 GB Galaxy Tab S11 on 2026-11-11. That is $100 more than ChatGPT's $899.99 card and $200 more than Tech Advisor's $799 link. At that price the S11 costs $450 more than Samsung's Tab S10 FE ($549.99) and $700 more than the Tab A11+ ($299.99). On top of that, Notebookcheck's Wi-Fi test ran the S11 about 11.2 h, against 17 h 42 min for the Lenovo Yoga Tab, which reviewed at $549 with 12 GB/256 GB.
standout_why: Pages compared: Tech Advisor 723363 (cited, dated 2026-11-10 on the page), iTechGuides' Samsung guide (cited, 2026-08-18) and ChatGPT's own catalog cards. Tech Advisor lists the S11 at '$799.99 when reviewed' with a $799 Samsung deal link. iTechGuides gives no S11 price, gives only the historical $499.99 MSRP for the S10 FE, and gives a SamMobile $349 figure for the S10 Lite. ChatGPT's card shows $899.99. None of them has Samsung's current $999.99 / $1,099.99 / $1,299.99 S11 ladder, today's $549.99 S10 FE or $399.99 S10 Lite prices, or any measured battery comparison between the S11 and the Yoga Tab. I couldn't open WIRED's gallery (fetch blocked) or the Android Central and Tom's Guide pages (truncated), so I couldn't check them.
decides: S11 stays 'best overall' on screen and S Pen. But at Samsung's $999.99 it now costs more than three times the A11+, and $450 more than the S10 FE, which is also a 10.9-inch Samsung. That makes the answer's 'Best value around $600' row the more important one. In Notebookcheck's test, the Yoga Tab bundle (keyboard and pen) ran about 6.5 h longer than the S11 on Wi-Fi. Against that, the Yoga Tab's update promise is weaker: 3 OS upgrades and 4 years of patches, versus the 7 years Tech Advisor credits to the S11. For buyers who can't stretch to $1,000, the page should give the S10 FE (our listed product) or the Yoga Tab, and say plainly what they trade away.
